audio_uri.description:
Audio file to be used as the soundtrack for the video. The audio sets the length of the
generated video, so its duration must be at least 2 seconds and must not exceed the
maximum the selected model supports at the chosen resolution.

| Model | Resolution | Maximum audio duration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ltx-2-5-fast` | 720p, 1080p | 20 seconds |
| `ltx-2-5-fast` | 1440p, 4K | 10 seconds |
| `ltx-2-5-pro` | 720p, 1080p | 10 seconds |
| `ltx-2-5-pro` | 1440p, 4K | 10 seconds |
| `ltx-2-3-pro` | 720p, 1080p | 20 seconds |
| `ltx-2-3-pro` | 1440p, 4K | 10 seconds |

See [Input Formats](/input-formats#audio) for supported formats and size limits.

camera_motion.description: Apply camera motion effects to the generated video.

fps.description: Frame rate in frames per second. See [Supported Models](/models) for available FPS per model and resolution.

image_uri.description: Input image to be used as the first frame of the video. Required if prompt is not provided. See [Input Formats](/input-formats#images) for supported formats and size limits.

last_frame_uri.description: Image to be used as the last frame of the video. Requires `image_uri`. When provided, the video interpolates between the first and last frame. See [Input Formats](/input-formats#images) for supported formats and size limits.

model.description: Model to use for video generation.

prompt.description: Text description of how the video should be generated. Required if image_uri is not provided. Can be empty string when image_uri is provided. If image_uri is provided, this describes how the image should be animated. If no image_uri is provided, this describes the video content.

resolution.description:
The resolution of the generated video in WIDTHxHEIGHT format. When omitted, the resolution is automatically determined based on the input image orientation — portrait images produce 1080x1920 video, landscape images produce 1920x1080 video. If no image is provided, defaults to 1920x1080.

Supported resolutions depend on the model — see [Supported Models](/models) for the full matrix. `ltx-2-5-fast`, `ltx-2-5-pro`, and `ltx-2-3-pro` support 720p through 4K.

duration.description:
Duration in seconds, defines the duration of the section to be edited
in the input video. Must be at least 2 seconds. The edited section can be at most
505 frames at the input video's frame rate (about 21 seconds at 24fps).

The section defined by `start_time` and `duration` should be within the duration of the input video.
If the section extends beyond the duration of the video, it will be clamped to the video duration.

mode.description:
Can be any of the following:
- `replace_audio` - Replace only the audio track
- `replace_video` - Replace only the video track
- `replace_audio_and_video` - Replace both audio and video tracks

The default value is `replace_audio_and_video` if not specified.

prompt.description:

defined by `start_time` and `duration`.

start_time.description:
Start time in seconds, defines the section to be edited in the input video. At least 2 seconds of video must remain after it.

The section defined by `start_time` and `duration` should be within the duration of the input video.
If the section extends beyond the duration of the video, it will be clamped to the video duration.

context.description:
**Advanced parameter:** Number of seconds from the input video to use as context for the extension (maximum 20 seconds).

The model uses context frames from the input video to generate a more coherent extension.
The sum of `context` + `duration` (converted to frames using the input video's FPS) cannot exceed 505 frames (~21 seconds at 24fps). For higher-FPS inputs, the maximum total duration in seconds will be proportionally lower; for lower-FPS inputs, it will be proportionally higher.

If not provided, defaults to maximize available context within the 505 frame limit while respecting the 20-second cap.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when the signed URL expires (1 hour from creation).

required_headers.description:
Headers that must be included unchanged in the upload request to cloud storage.
These headers enforce the file size limit and prevent overwriting an existing object.

video_uri.description:
SDR source video in HTTPS URL or base64 data URI format. See [Input Formats](/input-formats#videos) for supported formats and codecs.

Max frames (and max duration at 24 fps) depend on the input resolution tier — inputs are snapped to the smallest tier that fits by pixel count:

| Input resolution tier | Max frames | Max duration (at 24 fps) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Up to 1080p (≤ 1920×1080) | 181 | ~7 seconds |
| Up to 1440p (≤ 2560×1440) | 101 | ~4 seconds |
| Up to 4K (≤ 3840×2160) | 41 | ~2 seconds |

placement.description: Where the source video lands on the output frame: an **Anchor** such as `{ "anchor": "top" }` to fit and align it, or a **Rectangle** such as `{ "x": 0, "y": 0.35, "width": 1 }` to set its position and size exactly (see both below). The whole source is always kept and never stretched; the model generates the rest of the frame. Omit to center it at the largest size that fits.

resolution.description:
Target output resolution. The source video is extended to fill this frame. Pass one of the values below; each maps to an aspect ratio:

| Aspect ratio | Resolutions |
| --- | --- |
| 1:1 (square) | `720x720`, `1080x1080` |
| 4:5 (portrait) | `720x900`, `1080x1350` |
| 5:4 (landscape) | `900x720`, `1350x1080` |
| 9:16 (portrait) | `720x1280`, `1080x1920` |
| 16:9 (landscape) | `1280x720`, `1920x1080` |

video_uri.description:
Input video in HTTPS URL or base64 data URI format. See [Input Formats](/input-formats#videos) for supported formats and codecs.

Max 60 seconds and 1800 frames (e.g. 60s at 30fps, or 30s at 60fps). Width and height must each be between 64 and 4096 pixels.

VideoToVideoReframeRequestPlacement.description: Where the source video lands on the output frame: an **Anchor** such as `{ "anchor": "top" }` to fit and align it, or a **Rectangle** such as `{ "x": 0, "y": 0.35, "width": 1 }` to set its position and size exactly (see both below). The whole source is always kept and never stretched; the model generates the rest of the frame. Omit to center it at the largest size that fits.
VideoToVideoReframeRequestPlacement.title: VideoToVideoReframeRequestPlacement

VideoToVideoReframeRequestPlacement0.description:
Fits the video inside the frame and aligns it, e.g. `{ "anchor": "top" }`: | `anchor` | Where the video lands | | --- | --- | | `center` | Middle (same as omitting `placement`) | | `top` | Top edge | | `bottom` | Bottom edge | | `left` | Left edge | | `right` | Right edge | | `top_left` | Top-left corner | | `top_right` | Top-right corner | | `bottom_left` | Bottom-left corner | | `bottom_right` | Bottom-right corner | The fitted video always fills the frame along one axis, so an anchor only moves it along the other: 
landscape source → portrait frame
fills the width, so it moves up or down

 top       center     bottom
┌────┐     ┌────┐     ┌────┐
│████│     │    │     │    │
│    │     │████│     │    │
│    │     │    │     │████│
└────┘     └────┘     └────┘

portrait source → landscape frame
fills the height, so it moves left or right

   left        center       right
┌──┬──────┐   ┌───┬──┬───┐   ┌──────┬──┐
│██│      │   │   │██│   │   │      │██│
│██│      │   │   │██│   │   │      │██│
└──┴──────┘   └───┴──┴───┘   └──────┴──┘

████ = your video, the rest is generated
A corner anchor such as `bottom_left` works whatever the video's orientation, and a video with the frame's aspect ratio fills it, so every anchor gives the same result. Anchors other than `center` can't enlarge the video more than 2× its original pixel size, so they may be rejected for a small video; use `center` (or omit `placement`) to fit it at any size, or use a rectangle.
VideoToVideoReframeRequestPlacement0.title: VideoToVideoReframeRequestPlacement0

VideoToVideoReframeRequestPlacement1.description:
- `x`, `y`: the video's top-left corner, as fractions of the output frame (`0, 0` is its top-left).
- Send `width`, `height`, or both, as fractions of the frame. With one, the other follows the video's aspect ratio; with both, they must match it to within a pixel.
- The video must stay inside the frame, be at least one pixel on each side, and can't be enlarged more than 2×.

For a 1920x1080 video in a `1080x1920` frame:

| `placement` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `{ "x": 0, "y": 0.35, "width": 1 }` | Full width, top edge 35% down; height follows the video |
| `{ "x": 0.1, "y": 0.1, "height": 0.25 }` | A quarter of the frame tall; width follows the video |

height.description: Height of the placed video, as a fraction of the output height.

width.description: Width of the placed video, as a fraction of the output width.

x.description: Left edge of the placed video, as a fraction of the output width.

y.description: Top edge of the placed video, as a fraction of the output height.

VideoToVideoReframeRequestPlacement1.title: VideoToVideoReframeRequestPlacement1

| 16:9 (landscape) | `1280x720`, `1920x1080` |

get.description:
Poll the status of an async generation job. Status transitions through `pending` → `processing` → `completed` or `failed`. When completed, the `result` object contains output URLs (see each endpoint's documentation for the available keys).

We recommend waiting at least 5 seconds between polls. Choose a slightly different delay each time, for example between 5 and 6 seconds, to spread out requests when polling multiple jobs. Stop when the status reaches `completed` or `failed`.

Job status is available for up to 24 hours after the job reaches a terminal state, and can be removed sooner. Once a job is removed, this endpoint returns `404`. Output URLs expire independently of job status; download or re-host outputs as soon as the job completes. See [retention](/async-jobs#retention).

parameters.description: Job ID returned from the submit endpoint.
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: The endpoint type used when submitting the job (e.g., `text-to-video`, `image-to-video`, `audio-to-video`, `retake`, `extend`, `video-to-video-hdr`, `video-to-video-reframe`).
